```{r}
#| label: registry

# Standard: key on athlete id, never name (recruiting ids collide, decision 0013).
# The cfb_athlete_id here are the shared CFBD athlete namespace; each was resolved
# from the cleaned player_stats by name and QA-verified by its season/team pattern
# below; this post does not generalize the name lookup.
subjects <- tibble::tribble(
  ~who                 , ~cfb_athlete_id , ~gsis_id      ,
  "Arch Manning"       , "4870906"       , NA_character_ ,
  "Nicco Marchiol"     , "4685459"       , NA_character_ ,
  "Jordan Travis"      , "4360799"       , "00-0039797"  ,
  "Cam Ward"           , "4688380"       , "00-0040676"  ,
  "Trinidad Chambliss" , "4911529"       , NA_character_ ,
  "Joe Burrow"         , "3915511"       , "00-0036442"  ,
  "Malachi Nelson"     , "4870928"       , NA_character_
)
```

::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"}
*Data as of the `data-latest` release, retrieved 2026-10-17. Careers of recent
classes (Manning, Marchiol, Chambliss, Nelson, Ward's Titans tenure) are
right-censored; later seasons may not yet be present.*

## 1. Introduction

Widely held expectations about player careers are testable claims against
the data this project curates. This post evaluates narrative expectations
for seven quarterbacks commonly described with confidence: a
double-medical-redshirt transfer, a redshirt-then-transfer #1 pick, a
five-year quarterback whose career ended with injury, three multi-transfer
quarterbacks of the portal era, and the most heavily publicized recruit of
recent memory.

Each expectation is translated into a statement about what the database
should contain and evaluated against what it does. Results are reported as
a ledger, including cases where the data cannot observe the phenomenon,
which is itself a result. For each subject, a bolded redshirt verdict
states what the usage-based flag classifies, season by season, against the
expectation.

## 2. Data

```{r}
#| label: build-spine
#| include: false
con <- dbConnect(duckdb(), "data/cfb2nfl.duckdb", read_only = TRUE)
ids_sql <- paste(sprintf("'%s'", subjects$cfb_athlete_id), collapse = ",")

# Roster backbone + eligibility flags (derived table, decision 0021).
flags <- dbGetQuery(
  con,
  sprintf(
    "SELECT playerId, season, team, position, class_year, has_stats,
          redshirt_season, redshirt_career, fifth_year_career
   FROM roster_flags WHERE playerId IN (%s) ORDER BY playerId, season",
    ids_sql
  )
)
flags <- flags |>
  mutate(who = subjects$who[match(playerId, subjects$cfb_athlete_id)])

career <- dbGetQuery(
  con,
  sprintf(
    "SELECT * FROM career_summary WHERE playerId IN (%s)",
    ids_sql
  )
) |>
  mutate(who = subjects$who[match(playerId, subjects$cfb_athlete_id)])

college_picks <- dbGetQuery(
  con,
  sprintf(
    "SELECT CAST(collegeAthleteId AS VARCHAR) AS pid, year, round, pick, overall,
          name, nflTeam FROM picks WHERE CAST(collegeAthleteId AS VARCHAR) IN (%s)",
    ids_sql
  )
)
dbDisconnect(con, shutdown = TRUE)

# Usage: passing attempts per season from the long stats table.
stats <- open_dataset("data/player_stats.parquet") |>
  filter(playerId %in% subjects$cfb_athlete_id) |>
  select(playerId, season, team, category, statType, stat) |>
  collect()
attempts <- stats |>
  filter(category == "passing", statType == "ATT") |>
  transmute(playerId, season, attempts = as.numeric(stat))

# Game-level usage for the redshirt definition (section 2.1): regular-season
# games with any recorded statistic, and how many of each team's games the
# game-statistics table observed at all.
player_games <- open_dataset("data/game_player_stats.parquet") |>
  filter(playerId %in% subjects$cfb_athlete_id, seasonType == "regular") |>
  distinct(playerId, season, gameId) |>
  count(playerId, season, name = "games_with_stat") |>
  collect()
covered <- open_dataset("data/game_player_stats.parquet") |>
  filter(seasonType == "regular") |>
  distinct(season, team, gameId) |>
  count(season, team, name = "games_covered") |>
  collect()

spine <- flags |>
  left_join(attempts, by = c("playerId", "season")) |>
  # CFBD id reuse is excluded from career populations (decision 0022); assert
  # none of these subjects were caught by that exclusion.
  left_join(
    career |> select(who, seasons, teams, transfers, gap_seasons),
    by = "who"
  ) |>
  left_join(player_games, by = c("playerId", "season")) |>
  left_join(covered, by = c("season", "team")) |>
  mutate(
    games_with_stat = coalesce(games_with_stat, 0L),
    likely_rs = if_else(games_covered >= 5, games_with_stat <= 1, NA)
  )

stopifnot(
  nrow(spine) > 0,
  all(subjects$who %in% spine$who),
  !anyNA(spine$has_stats),
  # A missing attempts value should occur only on a no-stat (redshirt-shaped)
  # season; assert that, so the figure's "RS" label is never a lie.
  all(is.na(spine$attempts) == !spine$has_stats),
  # A season can only be flagged when its team's games were covered.
  all(is.na(spine$likely_rs[spine$games_covered < 5]))
)
```

```{r}
#| label: team-colors
#| include: false
teams <- open_dataset("data/teams.parquet") |>
  select(team, color) |>
  collect()
spine <- spine |>
  left_join(teams, by = c("team" = "team")) |>
  # FCS/D2 programs can sit outside teams.parquet; fall back to gray.
  mutate(
    color = if_else(is.na(color), "#9CA3AF", color),
    tooltip = paste0(
      who,
      " · ",
      team,
      " · ",
      season,
      if_else(is.na(attempts), "", paste0(" · ", attempts, " pass att"))
    )
  )
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-timeline
#| fig-cap: "Season-by-season college timelines for the seven subjects, in team colors. The number is passing attempts that season; 'RS' marks a season whose game-level usage is redshirt-shaped (at most one game with a recorded statistic among covered games, observable positions only). The hole in Trinidad Chambliss's row is a missing 2024; the database has no Ferris State roster row for the season he won a Division II national championship."
rel_lum <- function(hex) {
  m <- grDevices::col2rgb(hex) / 255
  lin <- ifelse(m <= 0.03928, m / 12.92, ((m + 0.055) / 1.055)^2.4)
  0.2126 * lin[1, ] + 0.7152 * lin[2, ] + 0.0722 * lin[3, ]
}
p <- ggplot(spine, aes(x = season, y = who)) +
  geom_tile_interactive(
    aes(fill = color, tooltip = tooltip, data_id = paste(who, season)),
    color = "white",
    height = 0.75
  ) +
  geom_text_interactive(
    aes(
      label = if_else(
        !is.na(likely_rs) & likely_rs,
        "RS",
        coalesce(as.character(attempts), "-")
      ),
      data_id = paste(who, season)
    ),
    color = if_else(rel_lum(spine$color) < 0.5, "white", "#111827"),
    size = 3.2,
    fontface = "bold"
  ) +
  scale_fill_identity() +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 2014:2026) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme_cfb2nfl(base_size = 14) +
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank(), legend.position = "none")
girafe(ggobj = p, width_svg = 9.5, height_svg = 4)
```

Figure 1 displays the resulting season-by-season timelines; Table 1 reports
the per-career summaries.

```{r}
#| label: career-table
career |>
  select(
    who,
    seasons,
    first_season,
    last_season,
    teams,
    transfers,
    gap_seasons
  ) |>
  kable(caption = "Career summaries from the roster backbone.")
```

### 2.1 Defining a redshirt from game-level usage

The redshirt flags below replace the stat-presence rule with a usage-based
definition built from the game-statistics table, which records which games
a player appeared in with a recorded statistic. Two properties shape it.
First, sampling coverage: a team-season with fewer than five covered games
is treated as unobserved rather than quiet. Second, how often a player on
the field produces a recorded statistic varies enormously by position,
estimated here among clearly full-time seasons (the top volume quartile at
each position):

```{r}
#| label: observability
#| include: false
gp_all <- open_dataset("data/game_player_stats.parquet") |>
  filter(seasonType == "regular") |>
  select(playerId, season, team, gameId, category, statType, stat) |>
  collect()
pos_of <- open_dataset("data/roster.parquet") |>
  select(playerId, season, team, position) |>
  distinct() |>
  collect() |>
  mutate(
    pos = dplyr::case_when(
      position == "QB" ~ "QB",
      position %in% c("RB", "FB") ~ "RB",
      position == "WR" ~ "WR",
      position == "TE" ~ "TE",
      position %in% c("OL", "G", "OT", "C") ~ "OL",
      position %in% c("DL", "DT", "NT") ~ "DL",
      position %in% c("DE", "EDGE") ~ "DE",
      position %in% c("LB", "OLB", "ILB") ~ "LB",
      position %in% c("DB", "S", "CB") ~ "DB",
      position %in% c("PK", "P", "LS") ~ "ST"
    )
  ) |>
  filter(!is.na(pos), !position %in% c("?", "ATH", "PR", "KR")) |>
  # one row per player-season (duplicate roster rows, e.g. mid-season moves)
  group_by(playerId, season) |>
  slice_head(n = 1) |>
  ungroup()
core_all <- gp_all |>
  inner_join(pos_of |> select(-team), by = c("playerId", "season")) |>
  filter(
    (pos == "QB" & category == "passing" & statType == "C/ATT") |
      (pos %in%
        c("RB", "WR", "TE") &
        category %in% c("rushing", "receiving") &
        statType %in% c("CAR", "REC")) |
      (pos %in%
        c("DL", "DE", "LB", "DB") &
        category == "defensive" &
        statType == "TOT") |
      (pos == "ST" &
        category %in% c("kicking", "punting") &
        statType %in% c("XP", "FG", "NO"))
  ) |>
  # C/ATT is the completions/attempts composite; attempts are the numerator
  mutate(
    v = if_else(pos == "QB", as.numeric(sub("/.*", "", stat)), as.numeric(stat))
  )
# season volume, then the share of covered games with a statistic among
# full-time seasons (top volume quartile) versus the rest
season_volume <- core_all |>
  group_by(playerId, season, pos) |>
  summarize(volume = sum(v, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
stat_rate <- gp_all |>
  distinct(playerId, season, team, gameId) |>
  count(playerId, season, team, name = "games_with_stat") |>
  inner_join(pos_of |> select(-team), by = c("playerId", "season")) |>
  left_join(season_volume, by = c("playerId", "season", "pos")) |>
  left_join(covered, by = c("season", "team")) |>
  filter(!is.na(games_covered), games_covered >= 5) |>
  mutate(rate = games_with_stat / games_covered)
observability <- stat_rate |>
  filter(!is.na(volume)) |>
  group_by(pos) |>
  mutate(full_time = volume >= quantile(volume, 0.75)) |>
  group_by(pos, full_time) |>
  summarize(rate = median(rate), n = dplyr::n(), .groups = "drop") |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(
    names_from = full_time,
    values_from = c(rate, n),
    names_glue = "full_time_{full_time}_{.value}"
  )
```

```{r}
#| label: observability-table
observability |>
  transmute(
    Position = pos,
    `Full-time seasons` = round(full_time_TRUE_rate, 2),
    `Other seasons` = round(full_time_FALSE_rate, 2),
    `Seasons observed` = full_time_TRUE_n + full_time_FALSE_n
  ) |>
  kable(
    caption = "How often playing produces a recorded statistic, by position."
  )
```

A game-level redshirt flag is therefore only meaningful where playing
reliably produces a recorded statistic: quarterbacks and specialists in
nearly every covered game, running backs and receivers in about half,
tight ends, linemen, and edge rushers in a quarter or less.

*Expectation: among those positions, the distribution of games with a
statistic separates low-participation seasons from full-time ones.*

```{r}
#| label: usage-fig
#| fig-cap: "Games with a recorded statistic per season, observable positions. Quarterbacks and specialists show a spike at one game, a plateau of genuine backup seasons, and a mode at a full season; running backs, receivers, and linebackers decline continuously from the spike."
obs_fig <- stat_rate |>
  filter(pos %in% c("QB", "RB", "WR", "LB", "ST"), games_with_stat <= 15)
ggplot(obs_fig, aes(games_with_stat)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 1, fill = "#2a6f97", color = "white") +
  facet_wrap(~pos, scales = "free_y") +
  theme_cfb2nfl(base_size = 14) +
  labs(x = "Games with a recorded statistic", y = "Player-seasons")
```

At every observable position the histogram is dominated by a spike at one
game with a statistic, and seasons with two or more observed games are
genuine backup participation rather than redshirts: a 53-attempt backup
season shows two. The adopted definition is therefore:

> A season is flagged redshirt-shaped if the player's position is
> observable in the game statistics (QB, RB, WR, LB, ST), at least five
> of the team's games were covered, and the player recorded a statistic
> in at most one of them.

The threshold is deliberately strict: it prefers missing a redshirt whose
few appearances produced statistics in two covered games over flagging
every real backup season. For unobservable positions (TE, DL, DE, DB, OL)
the flag reduces to the earlier stat-presence rule.

## 3. Results

### 3.1 Arch Manning, Texas: current player

*Expectation: playing for Texas, first in a reserve role, then becoming a
starter.*

```{r}
#| label: arch-table
spine |>
  filter(who == "Arch Manning") |>
  select(season, team, class_year, has_stats, attempts) |>
  kable(caption = "Arch Manning, season by season.")
```

**Redshirt verdict: 2023 flagged (redshirt-shaped, one game with a
statistic in thirteen covered games); 2024 through 2026 unflagged.**

The expectation is confirmed: four Texas seasons, 2023 through 2026. The
2023 flag is consistent with appearances held inside the redshirt window;
2024 is not flagged, and defining a "backup season" feature for it would
require an attempts threshold.

### 3.2 Nicco Marchiol, West Virginia then Northwestern: two expected redshirts

*Expectation: redshirting as a freshman at West Virginia, later taking a
medical redshirt there, then transferring to Northwestern.*

```{r}
#| label: marchiol-table
spine |>
  filter(who == "Nicco Marchiol") |>
  select(season, team, has_stats, attempts, games_with_stat, likely_rs) |>
  kable(caption = "Nicco Marchiol, season by season.")
```

**Redshirt verdict: 2022 and 2026 flagged; 2023 through 2025 unflagged.
One of the two expected redshirts is recovered (2022); the medical
redshirt is not certifiable from usage.**

Under the stat-presence rule the data show no redshirt-shaped season: five
consecutive roster seasons, each with a stat line. The usage flag does
better: 2022 and the injury-shortened 2026 season are marked. The 2023
season, with a statistic in two covered games and 53 attempts, is a real
backup season and is correctly left unflagged, the separation stat presence
could not make.

### 3.3 Jordan Travis, Louisville then Florida State: injury, draft selection, no subsequent NFL play

*Expectation: redshirting at Louisville, playing five years at Florida State
with the COVID season extending eligibility, suffering a late-season injury
in his final year, being drafted anyway, and never playing another NFL snap.*

```{r}
#| label: travis-table
spine |>
  filter(who == "Jordan Travis") |>
  select(season, team, has_stats, attempts) |>
  kable(caption = "Jordan Travis, season by season. Note two rows for 2021.")
```

**Redshirt verdict: 2018 flagged, but the flag is contradicted by the
external record (he played, 14 attempts); the expected Louisville
redshirt is not confirmed.**

The expectation is mostly confirmed, with one correction and one artifact.
The correction: Louisville, where he did not redshirt, he played. The usage
flag over-marks 2018 anyway, one game with a statistic in twelve covered
games, illustrating what the flag cannot see: appearances that produce no
statistic. The more precise account is a mid-career transfer after a
reserve season. The 2019 Florida State season shows 11 attempts, consistent
with his own injury year.

The artifact is more consequential: two rows exist for 2021, Florida State
*and* Louisville, though Travis did not play at Louisville that year, a
duplicate that propagates into every downstream join and indicates a
missing uniqueness guarantee on `(playerId, season, team)`.

The NFL outcome is unambiguous: drafted round 5, pick 171 overall, 2024, by
New York, with zero NFL player-stat rows across Jets rosters in 2024 and
2025. A roster presence is not a snap, and injured reserve also produces
roster rows.

### 3.4 Cam Ward, Incarnate Word, Washington State, Miami, then the Titans: the multi-transfer

*Expectation: playing for three schools, then being selected first overall.*

```{r}
#| label: ward-table
spine |>
  filter(who == "Cam Ward") |>
  select(season, team, has_stats, attempts) |>
  kable(caption = "Cam Ward, season by season.")

college_picks |>
  filter(pid == "4688380") |>
  select(year, round, pick, overall, nflTeam) |>
  kable(caption = "Cam Ward's draft slot (CFBD picks).")
```

**Redshirt verdict: no season flagged; the expectation makes no redshirt
claim, and the data agree.**

The transfer sequence is confirmed exactly: three schools, two transfers,
four roster seasons, selection first overall in 2025. His FCS origin is
where the data are weakest: no 2020 row at all, and 47 pass attempts in
2021 for one of the most prolific FCS passing seasons on record. Lower-
division origins systematically produce thin or absent early seasons, so
"career shape" features will misclassify players such as Ward and Chambliss
as late starters rather than as under-covered.

The recruiting table does not contain Cam Ward. He was genuinely unranked,
and "unrated" is a real category rather than an imputation target.

### 3.5 Trinidad Chambliss, Ferris State then Ole Miss: Division 2 to the SEC

```{r}
#| label: chambliss-table
spine |>
  filter(who == "Trinidad Chambliss") |>
  select(season, team, has_stats, attempts, games_with_stat, likely_rs) |>
  kable(caption = "Trinidad Chambliss, season by season.")
```

**Redshirt verdict: unresolvable; the game-statistics table does not cover
Ferris State in 2023 (fewer than five covered games), so no usage flag is
available where the expectation implies one.**

Our expectation is starting at Ferris State (Division 2) then transferring
to Ole Miss. The transfers are confirmed; the 2024 season is not. The 2023
season carries a redshirt-shaped flag under the old stat-presence rule, but
the usage flag marks it unresolvable. 2024 is missing entirely. The derived
career summary records `gap_seasons = 1`, which is incorrect; that "gap" is
the season in which he started and won a Division II national championship,
a reminder that a gap flag over a coverage-limited table measures coverage
as much as careers.

### 3.6 Joe Burrow, Ohio State then LSU: redshirt, transfer, first overall selection

```{r}
#| label: burrow-table
spine |>
  filter(who == "Joe Burrow") |>
  select(season, team, has_stats, attempts, games_with_stat, likely_rs) |>
  kable(caption = "Joe Burrow, season by season.")

college_picks |>
  filter(pid == "3915511") |>
  select(year, round, pick, overall, nflTeam) |>
  kable(caption = "Joe Burrow's draft slot (CFBD picks).")
```

*Expectation: redshirting at Ohio State, then transferring to LSU and being
selected first overall.*

**Redshirt verdict: 2014 through 2017 all flagged; the expectation implies
one redshirt, so the flag over-counts by three.**

The game-statistics table observed twelve or thirteen of the team's games in
each quiet Ohio State season, and Burrow recorded a statistic in none of
them. Only 2015 was a redshirt; he was an active backup who recorded zero
of any statistic the feed carries. A season whose observable production is
zero is indistinguishable from a redshirt, so features built on the flag
inherit a known over-count.

His recruiting row is absent although the class of 2015 falls within the
recruiting table's span: a coverage or name-resolution miss on the #1 pick
in the data's own draft table.

### 3.7 Malachi Nelson, USC, Boise State, UTEP, then Syracuse: the other multi-transfer

```{r}
#| label: nelson-table
spine |>
  filter(who == "Malachi Nelson") |>
  select(season, team, has_stats, attempts) |>
  kable(caption = "Malachi Nelson, season by season.")
```

*Expectation: redshirting at USC, then transferring through the portal
repeatedly.*

**Redshirt verdict: 2023 flagged, matching the expected USC redshirt and
recovering what stat presence saw as a played season; 2024 also flagged;
2025 and 2026 unflagged.**

The transfers are confirmed exactly: four teams and three transfers, the
largest transfer count in this sample. The 2023 redshirt is invisible to
the stat-presence rule (3 pass attempts), but the usage flag recovers it:
zero games with a statistic in twelve covered games. The 2024 season, split
between Boise State and UTEP with little playing time, is marked the same
way.

## 4. Summary of findings

| Expectation | Data verdict |
|---|---|
| Arch Manning is at Texas now | Confirmed; 2023 usage is redshirt-shaped |
| Marchiol redshirted twice | **Partially recovered**: 2022 and 2026 flagged; stat presence alone caught neither |
| Travis redshirted at Louisville | **Contradicted**: he played there; the usage flag over-marks 2018 |
| Travis: 5 FSU years, injured, drafted, no NFL snaps | Confirmed; zero NFL stat rows |
| Ward: 3 transfers to the #1 pick | Confirmed, but FCS years under-covered and absent from recruiting |
| Chambliss: Ferris State then Ole Miss | Confirmed with a hole: the 2024 D2 championship season is a missing row; 2023 unresolvable |
| Burrow: redshirt then transfer to #1 pick | Confirmed and **over-flagged**: four quiet seasons marked, one real redshirt |
| Nelson: USC redshirt then 3 transfers | Transfers confirmed; usage flag recovers 2023 and marks 2024 |

## 5. Discussion

One finding from this analysis remains open in the pipeline:

1. **Redshirt flags require a usage-based definition** rather than stat
   presence; Marchiol, Nelson, and Burrow collectively exhibit every failure
   mode. *Adopted in this post's methods (section 2.1); still open is moving
   the pipeline's flags onto it.*

The database satisfied most of the stated expectations, the least
informative of the results. The informative results are the three modes in
which it is *structurally* blind: quiet usage, lower-division coverage, and
a corrupted eligibility column.
